key_insight: Independent price-based scheduling of EVs and heat pumps can synchronize flexible demand and create feeder peaks worse than uncoordinated operation.
engineering_relevance: Distribution feeders with high EV/heat-pump uptake may need coordinated control or transformer-aware tariffs to avoid overloads and undervoltage.
method: Simulated a rural low-voltage feeder with 97 buses and a 250 kVA transformer.
Evaluated 160 runs across seven scenarios, four seasons, and device penetrations from 0% to 90%.
Compared decentralized cost minimization, fixed schedules, central transformer-capped scheduling, and time-variable tariffs.
evidence_signal: At 30% penetration of each device, price-based scheduling drove the transformer to 253% of rated capacity, and up to 478% at 90% EV penetration, with first undervoltage at the feeder end.
watch_item: Results are feeder- and scenario-specific, so real deployments still need local grid studies and coordination mechanisms before relying on dynamic prices alone.
paper_title: Price-Optimized EV and Heat-Pump Scheduling Can Exceed Uncoordinated Feeder Peaks
